comments.text: Plan to photograph an exoplanet 25 light years away with 25km per pixel resolution (2020) This is fascinating. There is a plan to directly photograph exoplanets by sending a series of telescopes 500+ AU in the opposite direction of what we want to photograph and using the sun as a gravitational lens. We send out waves of these small telescopes to get pictures at various focal planes. This video has a good description of the paper: [VIDEO]

comments.text: This video linked by another commenter explains it quite well: [VIDEO] Basically, it's possible to generate an image of an exoplanet, but "retargeting" the telescope(s) to observe another object is not feasible. So you'd better make sure the target that the mission will focus upon is actually worth the attention it gets - but there are other planned telescopes that will be capable of generating data that will allow selecting potential candidates.

comments.why_zh: 利用太阳的引力透镜拍摄系外行星表面的迷人想法。
comments.quote_zh: 我听说过一个非常迷人的想法：利用我们太阳自身的引力透镜效应来拍摄系外行星的表面
comments.text_zh: 我听说过一个非常迷人的想法：利用我们太阳自身的引力透镜效应来拍摄系外行星的表面：[VIDEO] 它看起来不会像你见过的任何望远镜。一旦我们有了想要拍照的候选系外行星，我们就会发射一群自由飞行的、由太阳帆推进的卫星，让它们进入这样的轨道：它们会被从太阳弹射出去，沿着与目标系外行星相反的轨迹飞行。它们会飞到太阳引力透镜的“焦平面”，在那里，系外行星的光被涂抹成环绕太阳的一个环，这些卫星协同捕捉它。大概一次这样的经过还不够，所以我们需要多次发送这样的卫星群，就像一波接一波的浪。我喜欢这个计划的地方在于，它既超级科幻，但如果我们想做，我们已经拥有了实现它所需的所有组件。
comments.text: I heard about this fascinating idea of using the gravitational lensing of our own sun to image the surface of exoplanets: [VIDEO] It wouldn't look like any telescope you might have ever seen. Once we have a candidate exoplanet we want to take a picture of we would launch a flock of free-flying solar-sail propelled satellites in such an orbit that they get yeeted away from the sun on a trajectory opposite of the target exoplanet. They would travel to the "focal plane" of the sun's gravitational lens where the exoplanet's light is smeared to a ring around the sun which they collaboratively capture. Probably one such a pass wouldn't be enough, so we would need to send such flocks multiple times, like waves following on each other. What I love about the plan is that it is both super scifi, yet we already have all the components to make it happen if we want to.
